# Clusterbuck

> A LAN-first LLM broker for client applications. It provides an OpenAI-compatible
> synchronous endpoint for interactive work and a durable HTTP job queue for work
> that may wait for an available or sleeping worker.

## Client integration

- [README](README.md): deployment overview, the two execution paths, and reachability rules.
- [Protocol contract](docs/protocols.md): authoritative prose contract for every request, response, state, and retry rule.
- [System design](docs/design.md): routing, privacy, capability scoring, waking, and cloud-fallback design.
- [JSON schemas](contract/): machine-readable contracts for async jobs and worker results.

## Connection and authentication

Set the coordinator's base URL, for example `http://coordinator.lan:8018`.
All API routes except documented health/static/bootstrap/worker routes require the
operator key when `CBK_API_KEY` is configured. Send either:

```http
X-CBK-Api-Key: <key>
```

or `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Treat this as an operator credential: it is
authentication, not per-client authorisation. Do not put it in a URL.

## Choose an execution path

Use the synchronous path only when a person is waiting and a reachable model server
is expected to answer immediately. It is OpenAI Chat Completions compatible:

```http
POST /v1/chat/completions
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "8b-extract",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarise this text."}],
  "temperature": 0.2,
  "max_tokens": 500
}
```

The `model` is a Clusterbuck capability alias, not necessarily the underlying model
name. Discover currently registered aliases with `GET /v1/models`. A successful
response is a normal OpenAI-style chat completion. A `502` means the coordinator
could not complete the request through the synchronous model-server route; do not
assume that means the async worker route is unavailable.

Use the asynchronous path for batch work, long-running work, or requests that may
wait for capacity. It is the correct route when a sleeping worker may be woken or a
job should survive a client disconnect.

```http
POST /jobs
Idempotency-Key: <new-opaque-key-for-this-logical-call>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "task_class": "summarize",
  "min_ability": 6,
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarise this text."}],
  "params": {"temperature": 0.2, "max_tokens": 500},
  "urgency": "waitable",
  "privacy": "local_only",
  "deadline": "2026-09-23T12:00:00Z",
  "submitter": {"app": "my-client", "request_id": "req_123"}
}
```

The asynchronous request must use exactly one addressing method:

- Preferred: `task_class` plus `min_ability`, so Clusterbuck selects a measured,
  sufficiently capable artifact.
- Advanced: `capability`, such as `8b-extract` or `30b-reason`, to select a
  supply-side tier directly.

`privacy` defaults to `local_only`; that setting never allows cloud routing. Set
`cloud_ok` only when the data and budget policy allow a hosted provider. Use `urgent`,
`necessary`, or `waitable` for `urgency`. Give user-visible work a `deadline` and/or
`escalate_after_min`: a waitable job with neither may wait indefinitely.

## Poll, persist, and cancel async work

`POST /jobs` returns `202` with `{ "id", "result_key", "status": "queued" }`.
Poll `GET /jobs/{id}` until `status` is terminal: `done`, `failed`, `expired`, or
`cancelled`. A completed job returns its OpenAI-style chat completion in `result`.
Persist that result immediately if it matters: completions expire after
`CBK_RESULT_TTL_S` (24 hours by default).

`queue_position` counts only unclaimed jobs ahead of yours; `0` can still mean work is
in flight. `started_at` and `worker` are best-effort coordinator observations, so use
`status` as the primary state signal.

Use `DELETE /jobs/{id}` to stop waiting. `cancelled` guarantees the job never ran;
`cancelling` means a worker already held it, so its result will be discarded when it
finishes.

## Reliability rules

Use an `Idempotency-Key` on every `POST /jobs`. Reuse the same key only when retrying
the same logical submission after an uncertain response; a replay returns the existing
job and does not enqueue another. `submitter.request_id` is diagnostic provenance only,
not a deduplication key.

Handle `400` and `422` as invalid requests or unsatisfied routing requirements rather
than retrying unchanged. Handle `401` as missing or invalid authentication. For async
work, retry transport failures with the same idempotency key, then poll the returned job.

Never send prompts, completions, or credentials to Redis directly. Clients communicate
only with the coordinator HTTP API; workers pull queued jobs themselves.
